title: Normality descent through a module-split principal quotient
statement: Let $R,A$ be commutative rings with identity, let $\iota:R\to A$ be an injective identity-preserving ring homomorphism, and let $\rho:A\to R$ be additive with $\rho(\iota(r)a)=r\rho(a)$ for every $r\in R$, $a\in A$, and $\rho(\iota(r))=r$ for every $r\in R$. Thus $\rho$ is a retraction linear for the $R$-module structure on $A$ induced by $\iota$; multiplicativity of $\rho$ is not assumed. For every $\theta\in R$, one has $\iota^{-1}(\iota(\theta)A)=\theta R$. The induced identity-preserving ring map $j:R/\theta R\to A/\iota(\theta)A$ is injective, and $\bar\rho:A/\iota(\theta)A\to R/\theta R$, $[a]\mapsto[\rho(a)]$, is a well-defined additive retraction of $j$, linear over $R/\theta R$. If $A/\iota(\theta)A$ is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], then $R/\theta R$ is a normal domain as well, meaning a nonzero integral domain integrally closed in its fraction field. This includes $\theta=0$: a ring embedded as a module direct summand in a normal domain is a normal domain.

proof.text: If $r=\theta s$, then $\iota(r)=\iota(\theta)\iota(s)$ lies in $\iota(\theta)A$. Conversely, if $\iota(r)=\iota(\theta)a$, apply $\rho$ to obtain $r=\theta\rho(a)$. Thus $\iota^{-1}(\iota(\theta)A)=\theta R$. Write $B=R/\theta R$ and $C=A/\iota(\theta)A$.

source.place: Tag 0309 (definition-domain-normal); agent adaptation of the fractional ideal argument in Tag 033G (lemma-descent-normal), replacing faithfully flat ideal contraction by the given linear retraction.

proof.text: The formula $j([r])=[\iota(r)]$ is a unital ring map: changing $r$ by $\theta s$ changes its image by $\iota(\theta)\iota(s)$. Its kernel is zero by step 1. If $a-a^{\prime}=\iota(\theta)c$, then $\rho(a)-\rho(a^{\prime})=\theta\rho(c)$, so $p=\bar\rho:C\to B$, $[a]\mapsto[\rho(a)]$, is well defined and additive. Moreover $p(j([r])[a])=[r\rho(a)]=[r]p([a])$ and $p(j([r]))=[r]$. These identities prove the asserted $B$-linearity and retraction property.

source.place: Tag 0309 (definition-domain-normal); agent adaptation of the fractional ideal argument in Tag 033G (lemma-descent-normal), replacing faithfully flat ideal contraction by the given linear retraction.

proof.text: Assume now that $C$ is a normal domain. Since $j$ is injective and unital, $B$ is nonzero ($1_B=0_B$ would imply $1_C=0_C$). If $bb^{\prime}=0$, then $j(b)j(b^{\prime})=0$; the domain property of $C$ and injectivity imply $b=0$ or $b^{\prime}=0$. Thus $B$ is a domain. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fraction-field-lift] to the injective composite $B\xrightarrow{j}C\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Frac}(C)$. It gives an embedding $h:\operatorname{Frac}(B)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Frac}(C)$ with $h(a/b)=j(a)/j(b)$ for $b\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 0309 (definition-domain-normal); agent adaptation of the fractional ideal argument in Tag 033G (lemma-descent-normal), replacing faithfully flat ideal contraction by the given linear retraction.

proof.text: Let $x=a/b\in\operatorname{Frac}(B)$, $b\ne0$, be integral over $B$, with $x^d+\sum_{i<d}b_ix^i=0$. Applying the ring map $h$ gives $h(x)^d+\sum_{i<d}j(b_i)h(x)^i=0$ in $\operatorname{Frac}(C)$. This is a monic equation over $C$. Since $C$ is normal, [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] gives $c\in C$ with $h(x)=c$. Hence $j(a)=j(b)c$ in $\operatorname{Frac}(C)$ and therefore in $C$, whose canonical inclusion in its fraction field is injective.

source.place: Tag 0309 (definition-domain-normal); agent adaptation of the fractional ideal argument in Tag 033G (lemma-descent-normal), replacing faithfully flat ideal contraction by the given linear retraction.

proof.text: Apply the additive $B$-linear retraction $p$ of step 2 to $j(a)=j(b)c$. This yields $a=bp(c)$ in $B$, so $x=a/b=p(c)\in B$. Every fraction integral over $B$ therefore belongs to $B$; by [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], $B$ is a normal domain. The fractional argument only uses an injective unital ring map with an additive linear retraction, so apply that same argument directly to $R\to A$ and $\rho$ to prove the final assertion.
